entries.candidate: Project Maize data center campus (Lavender Fields Holdings LLC / Phoenix Investors), former Federal-Mogul plant, 402 Royal Road, Michigan City, LaPorte County, Indiana; possibly Google's Michigan City site
entries.status_candidate: announced (physical conversion works evident but not observed in window)
entries.reason: Not in the Atlas. The City of Michigan City's Project Maize page (published 12 November 2025, modified 21 October 2026; capture mcin-project-maize.html) describes the redevelopment of the vacant 380,000-400,000 sq ft Federal-Mogul building at 402 Royal Road into a data center campus by Phoenix Investors and an unnamed end-user, and lists building permits BP-25-0492 (interior demolition) to BP-25-2858 (HVAC ductwork), IDEM air-permit papers and stockpile records. The September 2025 council resolution and taxpayer agreement (mcin-taxpayer-agreement-maize.pdf, OCR) name Lavender Fields Holdings LLC as developer and operator of 'Project Maize', a data center campus. IDEM's notice of 24 September 2026 (posted by the city 12 October; mcin-idem-notice-lavender-fields-20261012.pdf, OCR) opens comment on a significant modification of the source's Part 70 permit (issued 19 March 2026) to add 67 diesel critical emergency generators at 402 Royal Road; an extension notice followed on 20 October. That is a dated government record for the project, but air permits are ancillary, and the 2025-2026 building permits and May 2026 stockpile records show conversion works already under way, so an announced status would understate the project, while no in-window record observes the works. Google's Indiana page says Google announced a Michigan City data center location in 2026 and its Michigan City Data Center Advisory Council page (published 8 September 2026) speaks of its growing presence there, but no record found ties Google to Lavender Fields Holdings or 402 Royal Road. No LaPorte County parcel geometry was retrieved.
entries.reopen_condition: A dated (within 85 days) city, IDEM or operator record observing construction, completion or operation at 402 Royal Road (for example a certificate of occupancy, inspection or construction update), plus the LaPorte County parcel polygon for 402 Royal Road; a Google or city statement naming Google as the end-user would allow a Google role.

entries.candidate: Amazon Data Services Wharton County campus ('Project Eagle', 13 buildings, outside Boling, Texas)
entries.reason: New evidence for the 22 October hold: Amazon's data-center community news page (capture amazon-dc-locations-news-1022.html) carries a 11 September 2026 item, 'How we're building responsibly in Wharton County, Texas', saying Amazon is planning a 13-building data center campus outside Boling, about 10 miles southeast of Wharton, and that site preparation is already underway. The locator is still missing: TxGIO's parcel service, swept in eight envelopes covering about 16 by 18 km around Boling (captures txgio-ident-boling-*.json and txgio-ident-boling2-*.json), returns no parcel owned by Amazon, VADATA or another entity with an Amazon mailing address, and TxGIO address points have no Eaglewood street in Wharton County. The land sale probably post-dates the 2026 roll.
entries.reopen_condition: A Wharton CAD parcel, county development record or permit with a coordinate for the Amazon campus while the 11 September statement is within 85 days (until 5 December 2026); then admit as site preparation.
